rulings.challenge_claim: One item challenges (low) that the declared false positive on the missing ketiv/qere disclosure is wrong: the note at oshb:Jer.3.7 is live, stands immediately before the clause the entry argues in prose, and carries the reading both witnesses render; secondarily, that filing the reign anchor under a date-frame signal key overstates it. The paired item supports the entry and confirms the same omission as a heuristic false positive, on the ground that the entry only paraphrases that verse's content and cuts no boundary there.
rulings.grounds: Same object, opposite dispositions; the bytes decide for the challenge and refute the declared false positive. The variant inventory carries exactly one note at MT 3:7, and the bytes show the unpointed ketiv beside the pointed qere, ותראה וַתֵּ֛רֶא (oshb:Jer.3.7, byte tier), standing immediately before בָּגוֹדָ֥ה אֲחוֹתָ֖הּ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.7, byte tier) - the clause boundary_rationale quotes in the second witness and lists at web:Jer.3.7 among its evidence refs. A rendered quotation covering a variant verse with no variant disclosure in any field of the entry is the condition this book's citation discipline warns on, and that machine warn fires here, on this entry alone among the four adjudicated in this attempt; so the omission is a live disclosure gap, not a heuristic artifact, and the narrower test the supporting item applies - disclosure owed only where the disputed word is quoted verbatim or a boundary is cut at that verse - is not the disclosure symmetry this book runs. Severity holds at low on the bytes: both readings are the same narrative verb, the ketiv differing by a final he alone, so no sense the entry relies on turns on the choice, and this unit's seams stand at Jer.3.6 and Jer.3.11, not at Jer.3.7. The secondary point holds as well: the anchor reads בִּימֵי֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.3.6, byte tier), an in-the-days-of construction naming a single reign, not the year-formula or bet-plus-cardinal shape that defines this book's byte-derived date-header object, whose 19 candidate sites do not include this verse - so both halves of the date_frame.reign_sequence key overstate the signal. The seam warrant is untouched: the fresh speech-introduction verb with the addressee turn to the prophet is byte-true and remains the driver.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the ketiv/qere disclosure for the one note at MT 3:7 (single-witness), naming the qere as the reading both witnesses carry and stating that this unit's seams do not turn on it; keep the existing petuchah disclosure unchanged. observed_substrate_signals: drop date_frame.reign_sequence - the byte-derived date-header object does not carry this site and the verse names one reign, not a sequence - and leave the reign anchor in boundary_rationale prose only; narrative_frame.addressee_shift stays, so this is not a driver swap and unit_type, confidence, and strongest_rejected_alternative do not re-open. Tests the cure must pass: the entry must no longer carry a rendered quotation covering a variant verse with no variant disclosure in any field (the condition that raised the original warn), and every retained substrate key must name a signal the byte-derived inventories carry at this site.

rulings.challenge_claim: One item challenges (high) that the one-unit warrant rests on a blanket no-imperative and no-addressee-shift statement the pointed bytes contradict twice inside the span; that the doubled ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.3.19, the verse the rejected rival turns on, is undisclosed; that the rival is dismissed on a translation-side ground with its Hebrew pivot unquoted; and that splice and gloss extents part company at oshb:Jer.3.12. The paired item supports the same entry, holding that neither the imperative at Jer.3.12 nor the call at Jer.3.14 carries a fresh addressee, formula, or scene change, and that the Jer.3.19 rival was correctly declined.
rulings.grounds: Same object, opposite dispositions, and the bytes decide for the challenge. boundary_rationale claims that no fresh formula, imperative, or addressee divides the restoration promise and the reflection from the invitation that opens the unit; two of its three terms are byte-false. אַ֚ךְ דְּעִ֣י עֲוֺנֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier) is a fresh feminine-singular imperative, and שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) is a fresh plural imperative with a fresh plural vocative against the feminine-singular addressee of שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier). The plural second person in fact already stands inside the earlier verse's own tail, וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier) - one verse earlier than the challenge locates the shift - and the second witness renders all of it number-blind. The third term holds: no word-event formula and no messenger-formula onset falls inside Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20, so the cure is a re-cut of the negative, not its reversal. The variant point holds too: the inventory carries two notes at MT 3:19, one of this book's twelve doubled-note verses, and the bytes give תקראו תִּקְרְאִי and תשובו תָשֽׁוּבִי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier) - two second-person number alternations sitting on exactly the addressee question the cohesion sentence gets wrong, in the one verse the rejected alternative is built on, disclosed in no field. No count, slice, or rendered quotation covers that verse, so the mechanical disclosure arms stay silent there; the omission is material on content, not on the machine. The rival is raised on the rendering's fresh quotation mark, a tier-4 signal that is never evidence, while the Hebrew pivot at that verse, וְאָנֹכִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier) - the emphatic independent pronoun the entry names but never quotes - goes unweighed. Extent: the Jer.3.12 splice stops on the bound noun of נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier), severing it from the divine name, while the rendering beside it runs to the end of the verse; a second extent miss, named in neither item, runs the other way at the onset, where the splice carries the speech-introduction frame וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.3.11, byte tier) that its rendering omits. High severity is proportionate: the failed sentence is this unit's own cohesion warrant, and every further leg lands on the same addressee question.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the blanket negative with a positive cohesion warrant - the single divine speech opened at Jer.3.11 runs on with no onset formula anywhere inside the span - and state the imperative at Jer.3.13, the imperative-with-vocative at Jer.3.14, and the singular-to-plural addressee turn explicitly, with the disposition that keeps them inside the unit. device_notes: disclose the two variant notes at MT 3:19 (single-witness; a doubled-note verse), naming both as second-person number alternations, since the contested addressee reading and the rejected rival both stand on that verse. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-argue the Jer.3.19 rival from its emphatic pronoun-plus-perfect pivot rather than from the rendering's quotation mark, and name the closer rival at Jer.3.14; one sentence plus the mandated rival-disclosure sentence only. Splices: re-cut the Jer.3.12 pair so the rendering opens and closes where the splice does and no splice terminates on a construct severed from its nomen rectum, and extend the Jer.3.11 rendering to cover the speech-introduction frame the splice already carries. Tests the cure must pass: no negative claim about imperatives or addressee inside Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20 survives that the pointed bytes contradict (the test that killed the original); every variant verse the entry argues from carries its disclosure; each splice and its rendering share their opening and closing words. A re-span at Jer.3.14 is a PROPOSAL only, requiring explicit boss adoption - it is not author work.

rulings.challenge_claim: One item challenges (medium) that the renewed-call claim at oshb:Jer.3.22 is unanchored and untiered, since the same three-word call stands at oshb:Jer.3.14 on the far side of this unit's own front seam, leaving a byte-true device straddling that seam undisclosed; and, second, that the bare-heights noun is quoted here in its plene spelling while the same imagery earlier in the chapter is defective, with neither spelling named. The paired item supports the entry, holding the front seam a licensed speaker-and-scene shift with its mark statements exact.
rulings.grounds: The first leg is upheld, the second refuted. Upheld: שׁ֚וּבוּ בָּנִ֣ים שׁוֹבָבִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.3.22, byte tier) and שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) are identical at skeleton tier and distinct at byte tier - the noun's dagesh and the accents differ - and a skeleton-tier sweep of the three-word run returns exactly 2 verses book-wide, those two. The prior site stands inside the block this unit's front seam separates it from, so a byte-true device straddles that seam and argues continuity against it; calling the later site renewed names the recurrence without its prior verse and without a tier, and the byte-tier label carried by the splice proves the quotation, not the recurrence. Refuted: the spelling leg identifies no defect in this entry. Both forms are attested - the plene at Jer.3.21 (skeleton sweep: 2 verses) against the defective at Jer.3.2 (skeleton sweep: 4 verses) - but no field of this entry makes a count, recurrence, or exclusivity claim about that noun; the per-spelling discipline binds sweeps and recurrence claims, and the only claim attached to the word here is a verse quotation that collates at byte tier against its own cited ref. Severity stays medium on the surviving leg, which lands on the completeness of the front-seam warrant rather than on prose hygiene. The seam itself survives: the turn from first-person divine promise at Jer.3.20 to third-person narrated report at Jer.3.21 is byte-true, the setumah at MT 3:25 is the correct type, and the parashah and variant inventories are genuinely empty across Jer.3.21-Jer.3.25, exactly as disclosed.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale (or device_notes, if the disclosure is grouped there): replace the bare renewed with a verse-anchored, tier-labelled recurrence statement - the same call stands at Jer.3.14, identical at skeleton tier and distinct at byte tier (sweep: 2 verses) - and state its disposition: the shared call argues continuity across this unit's front seam, which is carried instead by the speaker turn at Jer.3.21. Tests the cure must pass: no recurrence adjective survives without its prior verse and its tier (the test that killed the original), and the front-seam warrant must still stand on the page once the counter-signal is disclosed beside it. No boundary change is proposed, and the spelling observation needs no field change.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two distinct items. One challenges (medium) a register lapse: pipeline part-and-row vocabulary standing in place of the literary self-reference, said to repeat across all four prose fields. The other challenges (medium) the parenthesis denying any address or formula shift at Jer.4.7 - holding that the second person turns from plural to feminine singular there and the speaking voice moves with it, while the entry keeps high confidence on that denial - and adds that the variant note at oshb:Jer.4.5 is placed on this unit's opening imperative when it sits on the verse's third imperative.
rulings.grounds: Distinct defects, not one: register on the one side, byte claims on the other. Both are real, and each item's own count-object needs correcting. Byte leg, upheld: the summons commands a plural throughout - הַגִּ֣ידוּ בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier) and שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס צִיּ֔וֹנָה הָעִ֖יזוּ אַֽל תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) - while Jer.4.7 turns to feminine-singular suffixes, אַרְצֵךְ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה עָרַ֥יִךְ (oshb:Jer.4.7, byte tier), a change consonantally certain in the final kaf where a plural addressee would carry mem; and the voice moves with it, from divine first person at כִּ֣י רָעָ֗ה אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא מִצָּפ֖וֹן (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) through third-person description to a first-person-plural speaker naming YHWH in the third person at כִּ֥י לֹא שָׁ֛ב חֲר֥וֹן אַף יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ (oshb:Jer.4.8, byte tier), before the divine formula returns at Jer.4.9. The formula half of the denial holds - no onset formula stands at Jer.4.7 - so the parenthesis fails on address, not on formula, and it survives only in the second witness, which is number-blind there and is tier-4 ground that is never evidence. The variant locative in device_notes is byte-false as well: the note at MT 4:5 rides on ותקעו תִּקְע֥וּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier), not on the verse-opening imperative that carries this unit's own warrant, while boundary_rationale states the same note correctly - so the entry contradicts itself across two fields. Correcting that item's own object: the qere sits on the fourth imperative form of the verse, third only under a bare-imperative object the item did not name. Register leg, upheld in substance with its object corrected: the pipeline vocabulary stands in three prose fields, not four - boundary_rationale (a writer part named as the thing that opens, and a following unit called a fresh row), strongest_rejected_alternative (a candidate split called its own row), and device_notes (three further uses) - while literature_type_guess is clean. Both cross-unit mentions do carry their verse anchors (Jer.4.10, Jer.4.7), so the verse-anchoring requirement is met and what remains is the workflow noun itself, headed by the part-level self-reference, where the sanctioned self-reference is the literary unit. The machine register arm does not fire on these strings, so the cure is an authored rewording rather than a validator-driven fix. Disclosure elsewhere is sound: the variant at MT 4:5 is disclosed and the pointed qere is the form quoted, the petuchah at MT 4:8 is the correct type and correctly held non-driving, and no paseq falls inside Jer.4.5-Jer.4.9.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the part-level self-reference and both row-nouns with this unit's own self-reference, keeping the verse anchors; and replace the parenthesis at Jer.4.7 with the byte state - no onset formula there, but the second person turns from the plural of the summons to feminine singular, and the voice has moved to a first-person-plural speaker by Jer.4.8. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-argue the declined cut at Jer.4.7 against that number-and-voice turn, not only against the absence of imperative, vocative, or messenger formula; one sentence plus the mandated rival-disclosure sentence. device_notes: correct the locative - the note at MT 4:5 sits on the trumpet imperative, not on this unit's opening imperative - and drop the remaining workflow nouns. confidence: re-derive it once the rival is weighed; high is not proportionate while the closest rival is declined on a denial the pointed suffixes contradict. Tests the cure must pass: no negative claim about address at Jer.4.7 survives that the pointed suffixes contradict (the test that killed the original); no field names a writer part or a row; and the variant locative matches the inventory's note position in both fields that mention it. A cut at Jer.4.7 is a PROPOSAL only, requiring explicit boss adoption.
